analysis.investment_thesis: INOX India is a genuinely excellent capital-efficient business (ROCE 38%, ROE 29%, D/E 0.10) sitting at the intersection of India's LNG, green hydrogen, and space/defense boom — but at 53x trailing P/E and 41x EV/EBITDA for a 12% revenue grower, the price leaves no margin of safety. Wait for a meaningful correction to the INR 900–1,100 range before building conviction.
key_strengths: World-class returns on capital — ROCE 38%, ROE 29% with near-zero leverage (D/E 0.10), reflecting genuine competitive advantage in cryogenic engineering
Multi-decade structural tailwinds across LNG infrastructure, green hydrogen, and ISRO/defense space systems — all priority sectors under government policy
Promoter holding at 75% with 50-year operating history signals strong alignment and institutional longevity
key_risks: Valuation is the primary risk — 53x P/E and 41x EV/EBITDA is extremely stretched for a business delivering 12% revenue CAGR; any growth disappointment will compress multiples violently
Free cash flow turned negative in FY25 (-3 Cr) with capex surging to ₹125 Cr — the high-ROCE story requires capex discipline to sustain
Net profit 6Y CAGR of just 2.7% (₹193 Cr in 2019 → ₹226 Cr in 2025) reveals earnings have barely compounded despite revenue growth; operating leverage yet to fully materialise
red_flags: P/E of 53x breaches my red-flag threshold of >40x without an exceptional moat to justify it — cryogenic equipment has competition from global players like Chart Industries and Linde
FCF turned negative in FY25 despite ₹301 Cr EBITDA — working capital or capex bloat needs watching over next 2 quarters
analysis.detailed_analysis:
INOX India is a niche industrial compounder with genuinely rare financial characteristics — ROCE of 38% and ROE of 29% in a capital-intensive manufacturing business is exceptional, and the near-zero debt (D/E 0.10) after aggressively retiring borrowings from ₹145 Cr in 2020 to ₹9 Cr by 2023 reflects disciplined management. The business sits at the heart of India's energy transition: LNG terminal buildout, green hydrogen electrolysers, ISRO launch vehicle cryogenic engines, and ITER fusion research. These are not cyclical tailwinds — they are decade-long structural themes backed by government capex. Promoter skin in the game at 75% is exactly what I look for in Indian industrials.

However, Rakesh Jhunjhunwala never pays any price for quality — and 53x P/E for 12.3% revenue CAGR is the market pricing perfection. EV/EBITDA of 41x means you're paying over 40 years of today's operating earnings. The recent capex acceleration (₹125 Cr in FY25 vs ₹44 Cr in FY22) compressed FCF to zero, and net profit has compounded at a disappointing 2.7% over 6 years. The recent trend (FY22–25 net profit CAGR ~20%) is more encouraging, but I need to see this convert into free cash before paying these multiples. This is a watchlist stock — I would accumulate aggressively around 28–32x forward earnings (roughly ₹950–1,100), where the India hydrogen and LNG story plus execution quality would make this a 3–5x compounder over a decade.
